;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**At least six civilians are killed when a minibus hits a [[roadside bomb]] near [[Mogadishu]]. There has been no claim of responsibility. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-blast/somali-minibus-hits-roadside-bomb-six-killed-idUSKBN23705U (Reuters)]
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**At least three civilians are killed and several others are injured in [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]] when a park comes under shelling from suspected [[Libyan National Army]] forces loyal to [[Field marshal (Libya)|Field Marshal]] [[Khalifa Haftar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/civilians-killed-as-park-hit-by-shelling-in-libyan-capital-idUSKBN2370O4?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria]]
**Hundreds of men on motorcycles, some armed with [[assault rifle]]s, [[mass murder|kill]] at least 18 people, including a local official in [[Sabon Gari, Kaduna|Sabon Gari]], and steal thousands of [[livestock]] in [[Katsina State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-nigeria-security/armed-bandits-kill-at-least-18-in-nigerias-katsina-state-idUKKBN2370S9?il=0 (Reuters)]
*A 20-year-old [[Kurds in Turkey|Kurdish]] man was stabbed multiple times by three men in [[Ankara]], [[Turkey]], killing him. The attack, described as a [[xenophobic]] [[murder]], was carried out as the victim was playing [[Kurdish music]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/killing-kurdish-man-turkish-capital-provokes-outrage-social-media (''Middle East Eye'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*Anglo-Australian mining corporation [[Rio Tinto (corporation)|Rio Tinto]] admits blowing up the 46,000-year-old [[Rio_Tinto_(corporation)#Juukan_Gorge|Juukan Gorge caves]] in [[Pilbara]], [[Western Australia]], on May 24. The firm issues an apology to [[Aboriginal Australians]] who are the traditional owners of the site, saying "We are sorry for the distress we have caused". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-australia-52869502 (BBC News)]
*A plane crash in [[Nettuno]], [[Lazio]], [[Italy]], kills two Italian competitive swimmers, [[Fabio Lombini]] and Gioele Rossetti. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/two-italian-swimmers-killed-in-air-crash (''Khaleej Times'')]
*A plane crash near [[St. Louis]], [[Missouri]] kills four people. [https://wcrz.com/grand-blanc-mount-morris-men-among-four-killed-in-small-plane-crash-near-st-louis/ (WCRZ)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda]]
***[[Rwanda]] reports its first death from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], a 65-year-old who had severe respiratory complications and was being treated at a specialised center. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-rwanda/rwanda-reports-its-first-death-from-the-new-coronavirus-idUSKBN23705A?il=0 (Reuters)]
**The number of worldwide confirmed cases of COVID-19 surpasses six million. The [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|United States]] remains the global epicenter, accounting for approximately 29% of all reported and confirmed cases in the world. [https://www.cnn.com/world/live-news/coronavirus-pandemic-05-30-20-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;International relations
*[[India–Pakistan relations]]
**[[Government of India|India]] expels two officials at the [[High Commission of Pakistan, New Delhi|Pakistan High Commission]] in [[New Delhi]], accusing them of being involved in [[espionage]] activities. [[Government of Pakistan|Pakistan]] condemns the expulsion and alleges that the two were detained and tortured by Indian authorities. [https://www.dw.com/en/india-expels-two-pakistani-officials-on-espionage-charges/a-53642472 (DW)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[Shooting of James Scurlock]]
***Police investigate the overnight shooting death of a protester, James Scurlock, by a bar owner in [[Omaha, Nebraska]]. Eyewitness video indicates the shooter was attacked by a group of people, one of whom was apparently Scurlock, before the fatal shots were fired. [https://www.omaha.com/news/crime/father-of-slain-omaha-protester-urges-peace-shooter-identified-as-downtown-bar-owner/article_0238d156-cea2-54b8-9a54-05e4e6e3ea42.html (''Omaha World-Herald'')]
**[[George Floyd protests in New York City]]
***A woman is facing four counts of [[attempted murder]], as well as counts of attempted [[arson]], [[reckless endangerment]], criminal possession of a weapon, and assault for throwing a [[Molotov cocktail]] at an occupied [[New York City Police Department|NYPD]] van during a riot in [[Brooklyn]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/samantha-shader-nypd-attempted-murder-george-floyd-protests (Fox News)]
**Rioting and looting continue overnight in cities all over the [[United States]] as 12 states activate the [[United States National Guard|national guard]] to defuse the situation. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2020/05/george-floyd-protests-police-brutality-intensify-live-200530231110124.html (Al-Jazeera)] [https://www.voanews.com/usa/national-guard-called-11-states-handle-protests (Voice of America)]
**At least 1,383 people have been arrested in 17 cities during the protests since Thursday. [https://news.yahoo.com/police-nearly-1-400-arrests-025906931.html (Yahoo! News)]
**During protests in [[Indianapolis]], two people are shot dead and two others injured after unidentified assailants open fire against protesters. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/indianapolis-riot-george-floyd-death-protest-demonstration-downtown-shooting-police-investigation (Fox News)]
**[[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces his plans to designate [[Antifa (United States)|Antifa]] as a [[terrorism in the United States|terrorist]] organization after saying they were responsible for the [[looting]] and [[arson]] occurring during the protests. Various [[government of the United States|government]] and non-government officials claim that designating [[domestic terrorism in the United States|domestic terrorist]] groups is prohibited by the [[First Amendment to the United States Constitution|First Amendment]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/05/31/politics/trump-antifa-protests/index.html (CNN)]
**The media is revealed to have been the target of violence and harassment at least 50 times on Friday and Saturday. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2020/may/31/george-floyd-protests-reporters-targeted-by-police-and-crowds (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro]]
**[[Post–World War II anti-fascism|Anti-fascist]] protesters gather in the [[Brazil]]ian cities of [[São Paulo]], [[Rio de Janeiro]] and [[Belo Horizonte]] in response to [[police brutality]] and [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro|Bolsonaro]]'s defence of unconstitutional measures. A pro-government crowd forms in São Paulo, with police reporting [[Neo-Nazism|neo-Nazi]] flags hung from a [[trio elétrico|sound truck]]. [http://www.therepublic.com/2020/05/31/lt-brazil-protests/ (''The Republic'')]
*[[2020 New Caledonian independence referendum]]
**In [[New Caledonia]], the largest pro-independence party [[Caledonian Union]] agrees to postpone the [[referendum]] on independence from [[France]] due to [[COVID-19 pandemic]] concerns. Anti-independence parties welcome the decision. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/417980/no-consensus-for-new-caledonia-independence-referendum-date (RNZ)]
*[[2020 Niuean general election]]
**In [[Niue]], [[Toke Talagi|Sir Toke Talagi]] loses his seat at the Common Roll and is now leaving his position as [[Premier of Niue]]. Former Secretary to Government Richard Hipa, a first-time candidate, topped the Common Roll votes with 440 and now looks to be a contender for the premiership. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/417977/premier-of-niue-loses-seat-in-election (RNZ)]

;Science and technology
*[[Crew Dragon Demo-2]]
**[[SpaceX]]'s [[Dragon 2|Crew Dragon]] [[spacecraft]] successfully docks with the [[International Space Station]] (ISS) with [[NASA]] astronauts [[Bob Behnken]] and [[Douglas Hurley]] joining the existing crew aboard the [[space station]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/05/31/tech/crew-dragon-docks-with-space-station-scn/index.html (CNN)]
